hook: SCP-3521 is a comedy, and it helps to know that up front, because it borrows the deadpan tone of a serious incident report. The joke grows out of a scrap of trivia pushed far beyond any sensible limit. Keep an eye on the footnotes; a lot of the humour lives there.
whyItMatters: The page is tagged with its author's name, dado, who also turns up inside the story as a character sending clipped text messages. It shows the wiki playing absurdity completely straight: the procedures are grim, the losses are real within the fiction, and the premise stays ridiculous. That contrast is what drives the piece.
thingsToNotice: The structure holds the explanation back: you see the result and the ruined site before the messages reveal the thinking behind it. The exchange plays like a two-person routine, one side growing more doubtful and the other entirely unbothered. Notice that the scheme misses its own stated goal, since the harm it was designed around is not what actually happens. The footnote about what the site was used for is a dry punchline placed right after the heaviest paragraph.

related.note: Another comedy that keeps a straight face from start to finish.
Dry clinical language meeting an absurd situation, with an uneasy edge.
